project.label: Project
project.title: Project overview
project.paragraph1: WearMask is a real-time, in-browser face mask detector built on YOLO-Fastest, trained with PyTorch, and run locally via NCNN and WebAssembly.
project.paragraph2: Both the deployment and training codebases are open source, with a peer-reviewed paper.
project.disclaimer: For research and demonstration only — not a medical device or diagnostic tool.

aboutPage.title: About WearMask | In-browser Face Mask Detection
aboutPage.heading: WearMask: In-browser Face Mask Detection
aboutPage.intro: WearMask is an open-source, real-time face mask detection system that runs entirely inside a web browser. The project is also published as WearMask: Fast in-browser face mask detection with serverless edge computing for COVID-19.
aboutPage.q1_body: WearMask (Web-based Efficient AI Recognition of Masks) detects whether people in a webcam feed appear to be wearing a face mask. Unlike cloud-based vision services, all inference happens on the user's device. No camera images or video are uploaded to an application server.
aboutPage.q2_title: How is it different from cloud vision?
aboutPage.q2_item1: Privacy: Camera data never leaves the browser.
aboutPage.q2_item2: Serverless: No backend GPU or inference API is required.
aboutPage.q2_item3: Edge computing: Detection runs on the user's CPU via WebAssembly.
aboutPage.q2_item4: Open source: Deployment and training code are publicly available.
aboutPage.q3_title: What does fully local inference mean?
aboutPage.q3_body: After the page loads the WebAssembly model, detection runs on each video frame inside the browser. The application does not send images, video, or detection results to a WearMask server. You can disconnect from the internet after the model has loaded and detection will continue to work.
aboutPage.q4_author: Primary author: Zekun Wang (ORCID · LinkedIn)
aboutPage.q4_inst: Institution: Vanderbilt University Data Science Institute
aboutPage.q4_support: Research supported in part by the U.S. National Science Foundation.
aboutPage.q5_item1: First public release: November 2020 (browser demo and open-source code)
aboutPage.disclaimer: Important: WearMask is a research and demonstration system, not a medical device or diagnostic tool. See known limitations.

limitationsPage.title: Known Limitations
limitationsPage.subtitle: Important boundaries and constraints of the WearMask system.
limitationsPage.disclaimer: Not a medical device. WearMask is a research prototype and public demonstration. It must not be used for medical diagnosis, clinical decision-making, or regulatory compliance without independent validation.
limitationsPage.sec1_item1: Performance depends on camera quality, resolution, and frame rate.
limitationsPage.sec1_item2: Poor lighting, backlighting, or heavy shadows reduce accuracy.
limitationsPage.sec1_item3: Small faces, extreme poses, or partial occlusion may be missed or misclassified.
limitationsPage.sec1_item4: The model detects visual mask-wearing patterns, not medical effectiveness or fit.
limitationsPage.sec2_item1: Frame rate varies significantly across CPUs, browsers, and devices.
limitationsPage.sec2_item2: Best performance requires modern Chrome with WebAssembly SIMD and threads support.
limitationsPage.sec2_item3: Safari on iOS is supported but typically runs at a lower frame rate.
limitationsPage.sec2_item4: Older browsers without WebAssembly support cannot run the demo.
limitationsPage.sec3_item1: Designed for research, education, and demonstration purposes.
limitationsPage.sec3_item2: Not validated for high-stakes public health enforcement.
limitationsPage.sec3_item3: Does not verify mask type (N95, surgical, cloth) or proper coverage beyond visual detection.
limitationsPage.sec3_item4: May produce false positives or false negatives in real-world conditions.
limitationsPage.sec4_item1: Trained on a specific dataset; generalization to all populations and environments is not guaranteed.
limitationsPage.sec4_item2: Model weights and architecture reflect 2020–2023 research; no continuous retraining is provided.

privacyPage.title: Privacy & Limitations
privacyPage.subtitle: How WearMask handles camera data, user privacy commitments, and known system boundaries.
privacyPage.sec1_body: WearMask performs all face mask detection entirely inside your web browser using WebAssembly. Camera frames are processed locally on your device. No images, video, or detection results are uploaded to a WearMask application server.
privacyPage.sec2_item1: Camera images or video are never stored or uploaded remotely.
privacyPage.sec2_item2: Detection results are never transmitted to backend databases.
privacyPage.sec2_item3: No registration, sign-in, or personal identification is needed.
privacyPage.sec3_body: After the WebAssembly model files are loaded, detection can continue even if you disconnect from the internet. The initial page load requires network access to download the application and model assets.
privacyPage.sec4_body: For the complete legal service statement (available in English, Spanish, and Chinese), see: Privacy service statement

researchPage.title: Research
researchPage.subtitle: Peer-reviewed publication and associated open-source resources for the WearMask system.
researchPage.paperName: WearMask: Fast in-browser face mask detection with serverless edge computing for COVID-19
researchPage.authors: Authors: Zekun Wang, Pengwei Wang, Peter C. Louis, Lee E. Wheless, Yuankai Huo
researchPage.abstractText: WearMask presents a lightweight face mask detection system that runs entirely in the web browser using YOLO-Fastest, NCNN, and WebAssembly. The design enables serverless edge computing: inference happens on the client device without uploading camera data to a remote server. This approach supports privacy-preserving, low-cost deployment for public-facing mask detection scenarios during the COVID-19 pandemic and beyond.
researchPage.step1: Clone mask-detector and install Python 3.8 dependencies.
researchPage.step3: Convert PyTorch → Darknet → NCNN → optimized NCNN following the repository README.
researchPage.step4: Build the C++ WebAssembly module from facemask-detection.
researchPage.step5: Deploy via GitHub Pages or run locally with python3 scripts/server.py.
